chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the child of adultery married?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, and the child of her (the mother) is not sought (for lineage attribution to the father).'

key_terms.وَلَدُهَا: Her child (referring to the child of the mother)

ai.seo_question: What is the marital status and lineage ruling for a child of adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the child of adultery is fully marriageable (muntaqah), dispelling concerns about inherent defect in their lineage. The key distinction lies in the principle of 'la yutlabu' (they are not sought), meaning the father is not definitively established for inheritance or nasab purposes, preserving the mother's lineage while allowing the child to marry into any family. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that zina does not corrupt the child's status for marriage, only affecting the paternal link.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A (female) child of adultery (bastard), can be married?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but do not seek her children’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain persons of our people from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:
“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about marriage with one born out of wedlock. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, but her children are not wanted.’”
